text: The crew could bring its regular pickup notes to the next hearing. No extra paperwork for anyone out on the road.
author: Codex writer B

text: Let the bottlers choose their stretch of road, but put its name in the minutes. I want us looking at the same ditch next session.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'll ask for the road name before we adjourn. Nobody should have to guess which stretch to visit later.
author: Codex writer B

text: Put the name in the minutes and the maintenance supervisor can check it against the crew's work orders.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'd start paying the refund now. The folks buying those drinks could bring the empties back tomorrow, and the bottlers could still send a crew out this summer.
author: Codex writer B

text: Would the bottlers still run the same trial? I'd like a chance to see what they can do on their own.
author: Codex writer B

text: I want to hear what happens on their stretch of road before we start taking deposits at every counter.
author: Codex writer B

text: Waiting means another season of highway crews working beside traffic. A refund gives people a reason to carry the bottle home before the crew has to reach for it.
author: Codex writer B

text: What does the crew think of letting the bottlers take over that stretch? I'd like the people doing the job to have a say.
author: Codex writer B

text: That's a fair question about the crew's hours. I'd ask the bottlers which days they'll send people out themselves.
author: Codex writer B

text: Watch the only clerk put lunch orders on hold to count a sack of cans. I want that shop to have a say in how much it takes at once.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'd want that limit posted at the door. The clerk should be able to point to it before anybody empties a sack on the counter.
author: Codex writer B

text: Take me through a lunch rush at that counter. At what point does the owner have to ask someone to come back?
author: Codex writer B

text: The corner market shouldn't have to call in another clerk just to get through lunch. Bring back a return rule the owner can manage.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'd like to hear what the owner does on the day someone brings in a trunkful. That's the day the rule has to work.
author: Codex writer B

text: When is there another pair of hands in the shop? I'd start with the clerk who has to call for help.
author: Codex writer B

text: Post a daily limit at the little market. The larger stores can take bigger loads, and everybody can start getting the refund.
author: Codex writer B

text: Where can someone who tops that limit go? In a small town the other store could be a long drive.
author: Codex writer B

text: Show me that the corner shop can set the limit itself. I'd want the person who works the till involved.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'd start the deposit and let a small store book a time for a big load. The shopper could unload when there's someone to cover the till.
author: Codex writer B

text: What about a shopper whose ride can't come again? An appointment only helps if the person can get there.
author: Codex writer B

text: Post the hours by the door, then. It's a long walk home with the same sack you carried in.
author: Codex writer B

text: By the time the bottle reaches the counter, the drink's long gone. I agree the cashier needs a mark that the customer can read too.
author: Codex writer B

text: It needs to stay readable after a trip home and back. I'd test it on the empty.
author: Codex writer B

text: Pass a sample down this row. Let's see who can find the refund mark without somebody pointing it out.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'd wait for a labeling rule. A family should be able to tell which empties are worth bringing back before anybody leaves the kitchen.
author: Codex writer B

text: That's where I'd try reading it too. Nobody should need the carton the bottles came in.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'd take the marked sample home and bring it back empty. If the mark's gone, we're still asking the clerk to guess.
author: Codex writer B

text: Print the refund right on the container. The customer can turn the bottle and read it, and we can get on with collecting the deposit.
author: Codex writer B

text: Where would the mark be on a clear bottle? I'd like to try it under the lights at a register.
author: Codex writer B

text: Has anybody brought a bottle off the filling line? I'd like to try reading the mark on one before we vote.
author: Codex writer B

text: Why wait? Show the refund mark beside the price on the shelf. Tell the shopper at the sale and I'd vote to start the deposit.
author: Codex writer B

text: The shelf is at the store. What would that shopper see when sorting bottles at home?
author: Codex writer B

text: Put the bottle beside the shelf sign. Can you tell from looking at both why the clerk paid on one bottle and turned the other away?
author: Codex writer B

text: That neighborhood store has handed over real money on a bottle from across town. I'd hold off too until somebody tells the grocer who owes it back.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'd have the distributors bring a sample claim. We could follow it from that shop to the company writing the check.
author: Codex writer B

text: That money is already out of the till. The store deserves to know who'll pay it back.
author: Codex writer B

text: Nobody behind the counter knows which truck brought a water bottle into town. Work out who pays across those routes first.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'd take the clerk out of the route dispute altogether. The delivery companies have the records.
author: Codex writer B

text: What if both distributors send the claim back? The grocer needs somewhere to go with those returned forms.
author: Codex writer B

text: The water distributors could settle the claims together. Pay the store, then check the delivery records. I'd support a deposit that works that way.
author: Codex writer B

text: Who puts up the money while those records are being checked? That's what I want settled before the vote.
author: Codex writer B

text: Put a name and a mailing address on that claim form. I'd take that back to the grocers to see if it answers their question.
author: Codex writer B

text: I wouldn't send a shopper across town carrying an empty water bottle. Let the store draw on a common account and start paying refunds.
author: Codex writer B

text: Which distributors have agreed to put money in that account? I'd ask them to come tell the grocers themselves.
author: Codex writer B

text: Who pays the grocer if the account comes up short? That's the promise I'd want in writing.
author: Codex writer B

text: The folks I represent want the refund. Think what a club treasurer could do with a sack of empties after a ballgame. The kids could put that money toward the bus home.
author: Codex writer B

text: A student saving for a school trip could tell what the cans in the garage are worth without waiting for a scrap price. That's something I can take home to people who want us to start a deposit.
author: Codex writer B

text: Back home there's support for putting a deposit on these drinks. Count the empties after a club supper and you'd have a start on the next trip. I'll vote to give those cans a refund.
author: Codex writer B

text: The people I speak for want to return bottles. A grocer ought to know when the cases will leave the dock. I'd let distributors send a truck around together.
author: Codex writer B

text: Why send separate trucks to the same grocery when the empties can ride together? That would make it easier to give people back home the return counter they want.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'll vote with my district for a deposit. On pickup day, let the driver take a mixed load. Leaving another bottler's cases behind wastes space the store could use tomorrow morning.
author: Codex writer B

text: People back home want a refund they can actually collect. Give the small store some say over how many empties it can count while customers are waiting for groceries.
author: Codex writer B

text: A shopper who saves a bag of bottles should know before leaving home what the little market will take. I'd allow a posted daily limit and vote for the deposit my district favors.
author: Codex writer B

text: It's possible to give people the deposit they're asking for and still let a clerk finish ringing up lunch. Let a small shop post how much it can take from one customer in a day.
author: Codex writer B

text: The voters I represent favor a deposit. Who counts the empties after a customer unloads them? That's paid work. I'd give the clerk's time a place in the handling allowance.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'm voting to start the refund people back home want. Before dividing the handling payment, separate the cost of marking a package from the time a clerk spends counting a return.
author: Codex writer B

text: Put the store's payroll beside the distributor's labeling cost. We can work out who ought to get the handling money while giving my district the deposit it favors.
author: Codex writer B

text: The district wants a deposit, and I'll vote for one. A bottler with a washer needs a bottle on the loading dock first. A refund gives the customer a reason to get the empty that far.
author: Codex writer B

text: Follow a refillable home with the shopper who buys it. What's the reason to carry it back empty? People back home favor a deposit. I'd make the refund worth that walk.
author: Codex writer B

text: A washer sitting at the plant does a bottler little good if the bottles never come back. I'll support the refund my constituents want and let the shopper start the return trip.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'd vote for the deposit my district wants. Give the customer a way to see which drinks qualify before somebody has to explain it at a busy register.
author: Codex writer B

text: A shopper can tell what's in a bottle while the label is facing out on the shelf. That's the time to show whether it earns a refund. I'll support the deposit people back home favor.
author: Codex writer B

text: People at home support a deposit. I'd want a cashier to be able to point to the drink that qualifies, even when the same brand sells something else in a bottle that looks just like it.
author: Codex writer B

text: The shopkeeper needs room to turn around behind the counter. A nearby shared return counter could give people in my district the refund they want without filling the aisle with bags.
author: Codex writer B

text: Put the return counter somewhere a person carrying empties can reach from the grocery. That's how I'd put the deposit my district wants into practice in a row of little shops.
author: Codex writer B

text: My vote's with the people back home who want to return their bottles. Let neighboring shops share a counter when the only open space in a grocery is the path to the register.
author: Codex writer B

text: Could the grocer help set the pickup day? Whoever sets the route ought to know which morning the stock delivery blocks the back door.
author: Codex writer B

text: Yes. Could a store call for that truck when the cases fill the stockroom, or would it have to wait for its day on the route?
author: Codex writer B

text: I'd take that offer to the smaller shops too. One truck doesn't do a grocer much good if the driver only stops for a full load.
author: Codex writer B

text: Put yourself in the driver's seat for a minute. Who signs for the mixed load when it leaves the shop? That's the piece I'd settle while the distributors are at the table.
author: Codex writer B

text: Then let's hear what the distributors need from us to ride together. I don't want to promise a grocer an empty stockroom on the strength of a truck nobody has agreed to send.
author: Codex writer B

text: That gives the grocer a single pickup to plan around. I'd like the shop to have one number to call, too, if the truck goes past with the cases still by the door.
author: Codex writer B

text: Give the shopkeeper a pencil at that meeting. I'd like to see the space the returns take up now and the path to the counter we're asking people to use.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'm glad you'd ask the corner shops. The person who owns the building may have a spare room in mind. The clerk can tell us whether you can get a bag through the door.
author: Codex writer B

text: Could we hold that meeting at one of the shops? When a grocer says there's no room, I'd rather look behind the counter together than argue over a drawing here.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'd want a customer there when we pick the spot. A shopkeeper sees a stockroom opening up. A shopper might see another stop to make on the walk home.
author: Codex writer B

text: Let's ask who'll staff that counter before we settle on an address. Sharing a room still leaves someone to count what's in the bags.
author: Codex writer B

text: And let the grocer bring the cleaning bill. Moving the bags out of the shop settles where they'll sit. It leaves the shared counter with the cleanup.
author: Codex writer B

text: Hold the empties side by side at the hearing. If the mark settles which one earns a refund, a clerk can show a customer the difference without calling the manager.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'd put that mark where somebody can read it on a full shelf. A shopper shouldn't have to turn every bottle around just to compare the price.
author: Codex writer B

text: That helps the person at the till, too. When two drinks look alike and just one carries a deposit, the clerk has something to point to on the bottle.
author: Codex writer B

text: Would you have the bottler put the mark on before the cases reach the store? I'd hate to leave a grocer sticking labels on bottles in the stockroom.
author: Codex writer B

text: That's worth doing on the bottle itself. A shelf tag stays in the store. It's at the kitchen sink that somebody decides whether to save the empty.
author: Codex writer B

text: Yes, and let's try the mark on a bottle that's come back wet. A customer can know what it's worth at the shelf and still have to persuade the clerk at the return counter.
author: Codex writer B

text: There's a reason I'd join the member on this. A school club can ask families for their empties after a game without asking anybody to reach for a wallet.
author: Codex writer B

text: That's a collection the kids can do themselves. They ought to know where they can take a whole carload before they promise the proceeds to the team.
author: Codex writer B

text: It would help to put a return point near the field. Otherwise somebody volunteers a garage and still has the bags when the season ends.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'll be voting yes. Give a little market room to set a daily limit, though. The clerk ringing up lunch may be the only person there to count the empties.
author: Codex writer B

text: Could the market put the limit on its phone message? A shopper with bags to carry ought to be able to check from home.
author: Codex writer B

text: Let the shop post the limit by the entrance. A customer who finds out at the register has already stood in the wrong line.
author: Codex writer B

text: The member has my vote. When we get to what it costs, I'd hear from the clerk who counts returns and the distributor who has to mark the packages. They do different work.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'd ask them to bring separate bills. That way we'll know what belongs to the shop even if we disagree about paying for the labels.
author: Codex writer B

text: Let's see the store's time sheet alongside the printer's estimate. One gets bigger as people bring bottles back. The other comes due before those bottles have even been sold.
author: Codex writer B

text: My reason for supporting a refund is the refillable bottle. The customer can start it back to the washer, if the bottler gives it a ride from the shop.
author: Codex writer B

text: Then ask the bottler to bring the driver along. The person who unloads the full cases knows whether there's room to take empties back.
author: Codex writer B

text: How far is that washer from the last store on the route? I'd want the return trip figured into what we're asking the bottler to do.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'd start the deposit. A grocer who takes back a water bottle shouldn't have to hunt down the delivery truck that first brought it to town to get the refund money back.
author: Codex writer B

text: Could the distributors settle with each other after the grocer gets paid? I'd like the driver to take the bottle without an argument over the route.
author: Codex writer B

text: Have the store keep its receipt for what went out of the till. Somebody can trace the bottle later without making the grocer advance the money twice.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'm ready to vote for the deposit today. If the bottlers have another way to get the empties back, there's still time to bring it to the floor before we vote.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'd hear them today. I'd also ask which stores and drivers have actually agreed to try what they're offering.
author: Codex writer B

text: Then let's leave time for that proposal when we take up amendments. The stores ought to be able to hear it and tell us if it would work.
author: Codex writer B

text: A refund I can collect only if I remember which store sold me the bottle wouldn't do me much good. I'd back the deposit and let the clerk go by the kind of drink the store sells.
author: Codex writer B

text: The clerk could show a shopper the covered drinks on the shelf. That's easier than asking who can find a grocery receipt from last month.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'd have the store post which kinds it takes. It saves a cashier from having to settle that question again with every unfamiliar brand.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'd pay the refund. I'd also have the processor talk to its buyer before the first load comes in. A buyer set up for flakes may have no use for baled bottles.
author: Codex writer B

text: Good. If the buyer wants the plastic ground up, we ought to know who's doing that work before we count a bale as a sale.
author: Codex writer B

text: Get the buyer's order in writing. Then the processor can price the grinding and hauling while there's still time to arrange it.
author: Codex writer B

text: I can support the deposit and still ask what becomes of a corner store's floor space. I'd have the grocer mark out where the returns will sit before we settle on a handling fee.
author: Codex writer B

text: Bring that sketch to the hearing. I'd like to see whether the bags will block the next grocery delivery.
author: Codex writer B

text: And ask for the cleanup cost on its own line. A drawing tells us how much room the grocer gives up. It won't show the time spent sweeping out that corner.
author: Codex writer B

text: I brought this bill here with a school collection in mind. A parent can leave the empties at practice, and the kids can turn them in for the trip home from a tournament.
author: Codex writer B

text: As sponsor, I'd welcome an amendment on the handling fee. Show me where a corner grocer can stack wet bottles without losing the aisle to the stockroom.
author: Codex writer B

text: What do I want the cashier to do with a bottle she doesn't recognize? Check what kind of drink it held. That's the rule I'd defend as the member bringing this bill.
author: Codex writer B

text: I put the deposit before this chamber because I'd like a refillable bottle to make it all the way back to the washer. Taking it across the counter gets us only as far as the stockroom.
author: Codex writer B

text: If there's a better way to get empties onto a truck, bring me the amendment. My reason for sponsoring the deposit is to get those bottles moving out of the shop again.
author: Codex writer B

text: Will the buyer take a bale as it comes off the press? As the member who brought the deposit here, I'd like an answer before we tell a town what its collected plastic will fetch.
author: Codex writer B

text: My bill asks people to bring their empties back. It falls to us to make that workable for the clerk who has a sack to count and a lunch line waiting.
author: Codex writer B

text: Put the grocer's question to me. She paid out the refund and the truck on her route didn't deliver that water. I brought the bill, and I owe her an answer about how she gets her cash back.
author: Codex writer B
